context: Scatterplot of age vs cholesterol for 250 patients across 3 risk groups (Low/Moderate/High), with marginal strip+boxplot panels on the top and right axes, a brushable selection that updates all views, and an overall regression line with R² annotation.
first_impression: Clean and well-organized; the three-color Tol palette separates risk groups immediately and the marginal panels feel like natural extensions of the main chart rather than independent cognitive load.
what_works: The 3-category colorblind-safe palette (blue/pink/green) gives instant group separation in both the scatter and marginals; the strip+boxplot combo in the margins efficiently summarizes distribution shape and spread without adding a histogram's visual weight. Brush interaction updating regression + marginals simultaneously is coherent because all three views answer the same question.
what_doesnt: The top marginal strip at r=2.5 with 250 points collapses into a dense texture — individual group positions blur together and the strip reads as noise rather than structure. The right marginal boxplot renders a single pooled box (not per-group), which misses the group-level spread separation that is the main story of the chart; a viewer who brushes a region expects to see group breakdowns, not an aggregate summary.
